description: Backend: add the realtime multiplayer battle infrastructure and server logic. Create a NEW API Gateway v2 WebSocket API with a dedicated ARM64 ws Lambda (lambda/ws.ts), enable DynamoDB TTL on the existing single table, model rooms/connections/players in namespaced items, implement the server-authoritative game state machine with server-side scoring (reusing the stored answerIndex, never exposing it), and gate host-only actions behind Cognito JWT verification while participants join with name+roomId only. Extend both test suites. The existing HTTP API, its 7 routes, JWT authorizer, Cognito, and quiz item shapes must remain UNCHANGED. This feature is independent of the frontend feature (FEAT-003) except that FEAT-003 depends on the WebSocketEndpoint CfnOutput and the message/action contract defined here.
steps: In lib/quiz-app-stack.ts, enable DynamoDB TTL on the existing `table` by adding `timeToLiveAttribute: 'ttl'` to the dynamodb.Table props (keep pk/sk, PAY_PER_REQUEST, RemovalPolicy.DESTROY unchanged). This is additive and does not alter existing item shapes.

In lib/quiz-app-stack.ts, add a NEW NodejsFunction `WsFunction` mirroring ApiFunction's config (runtime NODEJS_22_X, architecture ARM_64, memorySize 256, timeout 10s, bundling {minify:true, target:'node22', externalModules:['@aws-sdk/*']}) with entry path.join(__dirname,'..','lambda','ws.ts'), handler 'handler'. Env vars: TABLE_NAME (table.tableName), ALLOWED_ORIGIN (allowedOrigin), plus the Cognito issuer URL and the app client id (userPoolClient.userPoolClientId) so the ws handler can verify host JWTs. Grant table.grantReadWriteData(wsFunction).

In lib/quiz-app-stack.ts, import WebSocketApi + WebSocketStage from aws-cdk-lib/aws-apigatewayv2 and WebSocketLambdaIntegration from aws-cdk-lib/aws-apigatewayv2-integrations. Create `const wsApi = new apigwv2.WebSocketApi(this,'QuizWebSocketApi',{ connectRouteOptions, disconnectRouteOptions, defaultRouteOptions })` all wired to a WebSocketLambdaIntegration on wsFunction. Add custom action routes via wsApi.addRoute('createRoom'|'joinRoom'|'startGame'|'submitAnswer'|'nextQuestion'|'endGame', { integration }). Create `const wsStage = new apigwv2.WebSocketStage(this,'QuizWebSocketStage',{ webSocketApi: wsApi, stageName:'prod', autoDeploy:true })`. Call `wsApi.grantManageConnections(wsFunction)` so the Lambda can PostToConnection.

In lib/quiz-app-stack.ts, add a CfnOutput `WebSocketEndpoint` with value `wsStage.url` (the wss://... URL) and a description explaining it is the battle WebSocket endpoint and must be set as the Amplify env var WS_URL (mapped to VITE_WS_URL). Keep all existing CfnOutputs.

In lib/quiz-app-stack.ts, ADD the public-app (index.html) callback + logout URLs to AdminAppClient so the battle HOST can log in from index.html via the same Hosted UI. Mirror the existing adminAppBaseUrl + includeLocalhostCallback pattern: add `${adminAppBaseUrl.valueAsString}/index.html` (and, gated by includeLocalhostCallback, `http://localhost:8080/index.html`) to callbackUrls and logoutUrls, alongside the existing /admin.html entries. Do NOT remove the /admin.html entries.

Create lambda/ws.ts. Handler signature: `export const handler = async (event: APIGatewayProxyWebsocketEventV2Model): Promise<{statusCode:number, body?:string}>` reading event.requestContext.{connectionId, routeKey, domainName, stage}. Parse event.body JSON for the `action` field on the $default/custom routes. Dispatch: $connect (return 200; do not require a token so participants can connect), $disconnect (remove the connection item and, if it was the host, mark room accordingly), createRoom, joinRoom, startGame, submitAnswer, nextQuestion, endGame.

In lambda/ws.ts, implement Cognito JWT verification for host-only actions (createRoom/startGame/nextQuestion/endGame). Verify the id token the host passes (obtained via the existing Hosted UI implicit grant) by checking the issuer (from env) and audience (client id from env) and signature against the pool JWKS (fetch https://<issuer>/.well-known/jwks.json and verify RS256; cache the JWKS in module scope). Reject host actions with an invalid/absent token by posting an error message back to that connection and not mutating room state. Participants (joinRoom/submitAnswer) require NO token.

In lambda/ws.ts, model DynamoDB items in the SAME table, namespaced so existing QUIZ# items are untouched: ROOM meta `pk=ROOM#<roomId>, sk=META` (fields: roomId, hostSub, hostConnId, quizId, phase 'lobby'|'in_question'|'between'|'finished', currentQuestion index, createdAt, ttl); connection index `pk=ROOM#<roomId>, sk=CONN#<connectionId>` (fields: connectionId, name, role 'host'|'player', ttl); player score `pk=ROOM#<roomId>, sk=PLAYER#<name>` (fields: name, score, answeredForQuestion, ttl). Also a reverse lookup `pk=CONN#<connectionId>, sk=META` (fields: roomId, name, role, ttl) so $disconnect can find the room in O(1). Set ttl to now + a bounded window (e.g. a few hours) on writes.

In lambda/ws.ts, read the chosen quiz's questions from the table using the existing pk=QUIZ#<quizId> query (reuse the existing item shapes; may import a shared reader from lambda/index.ts or replicate the Query). NEVER include answerIndex in any message broadcast to connections. Implement server-side scoring: on submitAnswer, look up the current question's stored answerIndex and increment the player's score if correct; ignore duplicate submissions for the same question (answeredForQuestion guard).

In lambda/ws.ts, implement broadcasting: gather all CONN# items for a room and PostToConnection (ApiGatewayManagementApiClient with endpoint `https://${domainName}/${stage}`, PostToConnectionCommand) the current game state (phase, current participant-safe question, and the live scoreboard = participant names + scores sorted desc). Handle GoneException (410) by deleting the stale connection item. Broadcast on every state transition (game start, next question, end) and on scoreboard changes.

In lambda/ws.ts, EXPORT these PURE helpers (no AWS SDK calls) so they can be unit-tested: `generateRoomId()` (short, human-shareable, e.g. 6 chars from an unambiguous alphabet), `aggregateScoreboard(players)` (sort by score desc then name asc, return [{name,score}]), `nextGamePhase(current, questionCount, currentIndex)` (state machine lobby->in_question->between->...->finished), `toParticipantQuestion(question)` (project {n,text,options} dropping answerIndex, reuse/mirror toPublicQuestions), `scoreSingleAnswer(answerIndex, submittedIndex)` (boolean), and `validateJoinInput(input)` (non-empty display name + valid room id shape). Keep AWS-touching code in non-exported functions calling these pure helpers.

In test/quiz-app-stack.test.ts, keep ALL existing assertions passing and ADD: a WebSocket API exists (`AWS::ApiGatewayV2::Api` with ProtocolType 'WEBSOCKET'); the HTTP API still exists (ProtocolType 'HTTP') and its 7 route keys + single JWT authorizer are unchanged (scope route assertions by RouteKey / AuthorizationType so WebSocket routes do not break the counts); a second Lambda (the ws function) exists on arm64; the ws function's role has an IAM policy allowing execute-api:ManageConnections (search for the execute-api action in AWS::IAM::Policy); the DynamoDB table has TimeToLiveSpecification enabled on attribute 'ttl'; a WebSocketEndpoint CfnOutput exists. Adjust any resourceCountIs('AWS::Lambda::Function', N) style assertions to reflect the new function count.

In test/handler.test.ts, keep ALL existing assertions and ADD a describe block importing the REAL exported pure helpers from lambda/ws.ts. Cover: generateRoomId format (matches the documented alphabet/length) and reasonable uniqueness across many calls; aggregateScoreboard sort order including ties broken by name; nextGamePhase transitions across the full lifecycle including the final question -> finished; toParticipantQuestion NEVER contains answerIndex (hasOwnProperty + JSON.stringify scan, mirroring the toPublicQuestions test); scoreSingleAnswer correctness; validateJoinInput accept/reject cases.
acceptance_criteria: lib/quiz-app-stack.ts provisions a NEW WebSocket API (ProtocolType WEBSOCKET) with $connect/$disconnect/$default plus createRoom/joinRoom/startGame/submitAnswer/nextQuestion/endGame routes, a dedicated arm64 ws NodejsFunction, a WebSocketStage, a ManageConnections grant, DynamoDB TTL on attribute 'ttl', and a WebSocketEndpoint CfnOutput; the existing HTTP API, its 7 routes, JWT authorizer, Cognito pool/client, and quiz item shapes are unchanged except the additive index.html callback/logout URLs on AdminAppClient.

lambda/ws.ts implements the server-authoritative game state machine, host-only Cognito JWT verification for create/control actions, unauthenticated participant join/answer, server-side scoring using the stored answerIndex, and broadcasting of participant-safe state (never answerIndex) + live scoreboard; it exports pure helpers generateRoomId, aggregateScoreboard, nextGamePhase, toParticipantQuestion, scoreSingleAnswer, validateJoinInput.

test/quiz-app-stack.test.ts asserts the new WebSocket API, ws Lambda, ManageConnections IAM permission, DynamoDB TTL, and WebSocketEndpoint output, AND still asserts the unchanged HTTP API 7 routes + 1 JWT authorizer.
test/handler.test.ts imports and tests the REAL new pure helpers from lambda/ws.ts, including a test proving toParticipantQuestion never leaks answerIndex.
No answerIndex value is ever placed into a message posted to a WebSocket connection.
verification: User runs (networked host) `npm ci && npm run build` at the repo root and confirms tsc + esbuild bundling of both lambdas succeed.
User runs `npm test` and confirms ALL jest tests pass (existing stack + handler tests unchanged, new WebSocket/ws-helper tests green).
User runs `npx cdk synth` and confirms the template synthesizes with both the HTTP API and the new WebSocket API and the WebSocketEndpoint output.
Read lambda/ws.ts end-to-end and confirm no broadcast/message-building path includes answerIndex, and host-only actions require a verified Cognito token while joinRoom/submitAnswer do not.
